To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fox hunting by mounted hunts is an effective tool for the management of woodland habitat, and that the management has a positive effect on the conservation value of woodland habitat.
fox hunting with hounds has a measurable effect on woodland management and that the management of woodlands by fox hunts has a measurable effect upon woodland ground flora and butterfly diversity.
fox hunts in England and Wales manage 24,053 ha of woodland and other habitat for the benefit of fox-hunting, and that the management is beneficial for biodiversity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the contribution that fox hunting can make to the management of woodlands and other habitats in England and Wales.
the contribution of fox hunting to the management of woodlands and other habitats.
the conservation of biodiversity in woodlands and the countryside.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hunting with hounds in England and Wales is a countryside pursuit which has, in the last 5 to 10 years, contributed positively to the management of 24,053 ha of woodlands and other habitat.
fox-hunting in England & Wales is a significant contributor to woodland management.
fox-hunting in England contributes to woodland management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

fox-hunting with hounds has a small positive contribution to woodland and other habitat management in England and Wales, but that the contribution is likely to be small compared with the total amount of habitat management undertaken in the countryside.

the fox hunt management of woodland in England and Wales is a significant and under-appreciated contribution to habitat management, and the management of woodlands by fox hunts has positive effects on the conservation of ground flora and butterflies in these woodlands.
fox-hunting has the potential to make a significant contribution to the management, and therefore the biodiversity, of woodlands in England and Wales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fox-hunting in England is a widespread activity that is having a positive impact on woodland and other habitats in the countryside.

fox hunts in England and Wales manage 5.9 ± 2.4% of their woodland area, with the management benefiting woodland flora and butterflies, and that this is a contribution to woodland management which is little recognised.
the management of woodland by hunts has the potential to improve woodland structure and biodiversity, but the extent of the impact is limited to the area of woodland that is managed.
